_comment: The quality-tier ladder: decoration richness, and NOTHING else. It is a separate axis from the generator's renderer `rarity` (generator/data/rarity_renderer_architecture.json), which selects a rendering route. The two share their value names and mean different things; neither reads the other.

Common.intent: Plain by construction, not by luck. The pools are empty, so a Common roll cannot produce decoration even if it wants to.

Uncommon.intent: Introduces shape and cleaner materials, not ornament. At most one very small surface mark.

Rare.intent: Nicer material plus one small readable accent and a subtle motif.

RarePlus.intent: The premium presentation: best palettes, a special trim and one strong readable decoration.

budget_note: max_decor_cells is per view and was measured against the real decal footprints, not chosen round: a band is 6 cells and a small attachment 6-7, so a Rare hat carrying both needs 12. A tighter number would have silently refused the combination the tier is meant to describe.
floor_note: min_decor_pieces is a floor, not a target. The chance roll supplies variety; without a floor a RarePlus beret could roll empty and come out plainer than an Uncommon one, which the M2 batch caught twice. Common and Uncommon keep a floor of 0 on purpose: plain is a legitimate result there.
pick_chance_note: Used only by the weighted (profile) path: the chance that a tier reaches for a piece of a given kind at all, before the floor tops it up. The unweighted path keeps its original per-decal 0.62 gate untouched.
